description.narrative:
Internews har inkommit med en ansökan till ambassaden för finansiering av programmet "Improving Citizens’ Access to Public Information through Community Radio Content Syndication in Liberia (Radio Content Syndication in Liberia)". Ambassadens bedömning är att insatsen bidrar till uppfyllande av strategimål inom ramen för Strategin för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete i Liberia 2021–2025, framförallt genom att bidra till "Stöd för att stärka civilsamhället och media".
Insatsen syftar till att stärka effektiviteten och hållbarheten hos ett nätverk av lokala radiostationer (Community Radio Stations) att fungera som en kanal för medborgarröster och ansvarsutkrävande, genom två primära mål:
1) Öka kvantitet, kvalité och räckvidd av lokal radiojournalistik om aktuella ämnen genom innehållssyndikering ("content syndication") och informationsdelande nätverk;
2) Förbättra ALICORs och lokala radiostationers (Community Radio Stations) administration, organisatoriska kapacitet och finansiella hållbarhet.
Under den 36-månader långa insatsen kommer Internews möjliggöra för Association of Liberian Community Radios (ALICOR) att etablera och använda en multimedianläggning för produktion och distribuering av kvalitativ radiojournalistik genom sina medlemmar över hela landet. Internews kommer utbilda och stötta ALICORs sekretariat, genomförande kapacitetsstärkande insatser för deras medlemsstationer, och utveckla affärsmodeller som kan stärka hållbarheten och förmågan hos ALICOR.
Programmet är väl planerat och relevant med realistiska mål och mätbara resultat, såväl som en tydlig förändringsteori. Internews är en global organisation som Sida har goda erfarenheter med både globalt och i andra landstrategier. Insatsen blir ett viktigt tillskott till ambassadens portfölj innebär en hållbar väg framåt för radiojournalistik i Liberia. Ambassaden kan därför ingå detta avtal med förväntningen att denna insats kommer bidra till Sveriges strategi i Liberia.

Internews have submitted a proposal to the Embassy to support the programme "Improving Citizens’ Access to Public Information through Community Radio Content Syndication in Liberia (Radio Content Syndication in Liberia)". The Embassy assess that the proposed contribution will contribute to “Support to strengthen civil society and the media" as stated in the 2021-2025 Swedish strategy for Liberia.
The contribution aims to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of a network of Liberian community radios in serving as a conduit for citizen voices and government response through two main objectives:
1) Increase the quantity, quality and reach of community radio content on critical issues through content syndication and information sharing network
2) Improve management, organisational capacity and financial sustainability of ALICOR and community radio stations
During the 36-month intervention the Association of Liberian Community Radios (ALICOR) will be supported to set up and operate a multimedia facility for content gathering production and distribution of high-quality processed radio programs broadcast through their member radios with nationwide coverage. In addition to setting up the media facility, Internews will train and support ALICOR staff and members to strengthen their secretariat, prepare members for participating in the joint radio production, and develop business models which will promote the sustainability and longevity of ALICOR, and their ability to continue sending radio nation-wide.
The programme is well planned and relevant with achievable and measurable outcomes and a clear Theory of Change. Internews is a global organisation which Sida has previous experience with. This contribution will be an important addition to the current portfolio presenting a sustainable way forward for support to radio-journalism in Liberia. The Embassy can therefore enter this agreement confident that this contribution has very good potential to contribute to the Swedish strategy for Liberia.

The main goal of this project was to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of a network of Liberian community radios in serving as a conduit for citizen voices and government response, through two intertwined objectives:
1) Increase the quantity, quality and reach of community radio content on critical issues through content syndication and information sharing network
2) Improve management, organisational capacity and financial sustainability of ALICOR and community radio stations
This was to be achieved by Internews supporting the Association of Liberia Community Radios (ALICOR) to set up and manage a multimedia production center with ALICOR staff trained by Internews in multimedia content production. The facility will be utilized to carry out core activities under this project.

description.narrative:
This 36-month project, co-designed by Internews and ALICOR sought to enhance the production and distribution of multimedia content on critical issues and strengthen the financial and organizational sustainability of community radio stations across the country. To achieve this Internews supported ALICOR in establishing the National Information Dissemination Center (NIDC) in Monrovia, a state-of-the-art multimedia facility that has enhanced the way community radio content is produced and distributed in Liberia.
The initiative also focused on empowering rural and marginalized communities by providing timely, accurate, and inclusive information, thereby enhancing citizen participation and public accountability. The NIDC now serves as the central hub for syndicating high-quality radio programs to 30 community radio stations, reaching an estimated 338,578 persons in rural and underserved regions across the country.
Under objective 1, the project enabled the production and distribution of 96 radio programs. Among these were Citizens Agenda, which amplified citizen voices and addressed pressing community concerns; What the Government Says, which relayed regular updates and clarifications from public officials; and Elections Today, a civic education series launched during the 2023 general and presidential elections. These programs focused on critical themes such as health, governance, education, electoral processes, and community development. According to the midterm review evaluation data, 80% of listeners found the content valuable and informative, while 78% reported improved understanding of civic rights, electoral participation, and public accountability. Another 85% credited radio programs with positively influencing their understanding and actions, particularly regarding women's leadership, health practices, and local governance.
Beyond broadcasting information, the NIDC established itself as a reliable two-way conduit for information flow, enabling government messages to reach citizens and allowing public voices to be heard by decision-makers. This dynamic was particularly visible during the 2023 electoral period, when first-time voters, women candidates, civil society organizations, and electoral officials regularly featured in program segments, helping to foster a more peaceful, informed, and participatory election season in a context often marked by political fragility. Strong public trust in media accuracy was asserted, with 85% of beneficiaries affirming that community radio provides accurate information about government policies and legislative functions following the midterm evaluation. The outcomes under this objective include increased access to reliable and locally relevant information for rural populations, greater citizen engagement in governance and electoral processes, and strengthened editorial collaboration across radio stations through a shared syndication mechanism that amplified national cohesion and public trust.
Under objective 2, an organizational capacity assessment (OCA) for ALICOR was conducted in order to identify the specific capacity development needs of the organization. The findings from this assessment were used to inform its engagements with the Association to ensure that ALICOR is viable and responsive to the needs of its members and the communities . By the end of the project the OCA score had improved from 2.5 - 3.3, with 3 sustainability benchmarks achieved. ALICOR underwent a profound transformation from a fragmented, volunteer-based network to a structured and professional national media organization. With sustained technical support from Internews, ALICOR established a dedicated Secretariat responsible for daily operations, introduced core institutional tools including Standard Operating Procedures, financial and administrative policy manuals, and a Strategic Plan for 20232025. These foundational instruments significantly improved internal coordination, financial oversight, and program implementation capacity. However, the organization experienced internal turbulence including the resignation of two Secretariat heads and public allegations of financial mismanagement. An independent investigation commissioned during the project echoed previous OCA recommendations, identifying the need for stronger enforcement of policies, clearer definition of roles and responsibilities, and increased board engagement. These challenges were addressed proactively during the final year of implementation.
Towards the end of the project progress was also achieved in the area of financial sustainability. ALICOR successfully secured over $40,000 in media production contracts from high-profile partners such as Catholic Relief Services, the European Union, and ArcelorMittal. These contracts marked an important turning point, enabled by the rollout of a new business model and marketing strategy that positioned the NIDC as a professional and competitive service provider for media production. As part of its growth strategy, ALICOR also began expanding into online TV and other multimedia services, with the goal of further diversifying its revenue streams. As a result of these combined efforts, ALICOR is now recognized as a legitimate national coordination body for community radios in Liberia. The establishment of a functional Secretariat also enhanced internal governance, and the emergence of income-generating contracts have collectively laid the foundation for long-term institutional credibility and resilience.
